trace: PLTR's daily chart is the question here, and what strikes me first is the shape of the last 35 sessions: swings that widened, then narrowed. That expanding-then-contracting sequence is the anatomy of a diamond top, rare but tradable. Before committing to that read I want the indicator backdrop to be consistent with a coiling market, and it is. ADX(14) at 16.2 confirms trendlessness, Bollinger Band Width at 0.12 sits in the 15th percentile of its one-year range, and ATR has bled down to $0.85 over four weeks. RSI at 42.5 oscillating between 35 and 55 says indecision with a bearish lean, and MACD at -0.18 under a -0.15 signal line keeps momentum tilted down. I can draw the diamond's boundaries off the $26.10 and $25.40 highs against the $21.80 and $22.50 lows, giving a pattern height of about $4.30. The tension is directional: Stochastic is turning up from oversold, which argues against shorting, but I weight that as noise inside a consolidation; the OBV divergence and the bearish MACD posture matter more. So the plan should be conditional, not anticipatory: short only on a daily close below $22.50 with a volume spike, first target the 200-day SMA at $20.15, second the measured move at $18.20 ($22.50 minus $4.30), stop at $24.30 above the EMAs, which is $1.80 of risk against $4.30 of reward, about 1:2.39. I'd handicap breakdown at 65%, sideways 25%, upside failure 10%, and call conviction medium-high, 7 of 10, upgrading only on a confirmed high-volume break.

AMD just printed $184.92, a fresh high, but the oscillators refused to ratify it, and that mismatch is the crux of this analysis. RSI peaked at only 74.2 on the new high versus 79.8 at the prior $174.50 peak; the MACD line topped at +3.98 against an earlier +5.50, and now sits at +3.52 below its +4.15 signal with a widening negative histogram after a crossover three sessions ago. That's a textbook multi-oscillator bearish divergence, and MFI, OBV, and a CMF flip to -0.04 all corroborate distribution. The counterargument I have to weigh is trend strength: ADX at 48.9 is very strong, and price sits 45.2% above the 200-day EMA at $121.55, so the primary uptrend is intact. But that extension is itself the vulnerability — the gap down to the 50-day EMA at $156.40 is the natural magnet for a mean-reversion move, and ATR at $7.15 says any correction will travel fast. The resolution is to frame this as a short-term corrective short inside a bull market, not a reversal call. Structure helps: a double top at $184.92/$184.50 with a neckline at $172.50, which is also the 23.6% Fibonacci level. Entry only on a confirmed daily close below $172.50, targets at $165.00 (38.2% Fib), $158.50-$160.00 (50% Fib and measured move), then $156.40, stop at $179.50. That's $7.00 of risk against $14.00 to the second target, 2:1. I'd put breakdown odds at 75% and reaching $158.50 at 60% once triggered, which supports high conviction, 8.5 of 10, contingent on the trigger.

Looking at three months of AMD daily data, the divergence question answers itself fairly cleanly: price made $184.50 last week, above the $180.20 high from three weeks ago, yet RSI peaked at only 71.5 versus 78.5 at the earlier top, and the MACD line topped at +4.10 versus +5.20. Both oscillators failed to confirm, MACD has already crossed bearishly (now +3.50 under a +3.85 signal), and the volume tape agrees — the new high came on lighter participation, with OBV diverging too. The validation step the prompt asks for is therefore satisfied on all three pillars: momentum, volume, and price action, where the poke outside the upper Bollinger Band followed by a close back inside reads as a head fake. My hesitation is the trend context. The EMA stack is fully bullish — 20-day at $175.10, 50-day at $164.80, 200-day at $135.25 — and ADX at 45.2 marks a very strong trend; high-beta names like AMD can walk the band and shrug off overbought readings. So I'll frame this strictly as a pullback trade, not a reversal. The double top neckline sits at $168.00. Entry on a break of the 20-day EMA around $174.90 (or aggressively near $178.00), stop above the high at $185.50, targets at $168.00, then $164.00 where the 50-day EMA meets the 38.2% Fibonacci, then $157.25 at the 50% retracement if the neckline gives way. The math to Target 1 is poor (0.65:1), so that's a scale-out, with Target 2 the real objective at roughly 1:1. I'd assign 60% to the pullback scenario, 15% to divergence failure, and land at 8 of 10 conviction for a move to $164-$168 within one to four weeks.

RIVN presents almost no directional information right now, and that absence is itself the signal. Every volatility gauge I check is compressed to an extreme: Bollinger Band Width at 0.15 is in the 5th percentile of its 52-week range, ATR(14) has fallen to $0.55, its lowest in over a year, and the Keltner Channels are trading entirely inside the Bollinger Bands — a literal TTM Squeeze. ADX at 12.8 confirms there is no trend to speak of, MACD is coiled at -0.21 against a -0.23 signal with a negligible histogram, and RSI at 48.5 has been pinned between 40 and 60 for six weeks. The 20-day and 50-day EMAs at $11.05 and $11.20 have converged and gone flat. Price action gives me the structure: an eight-week symmetrical triangle with resistance at $11.80 and support at $10.20, apex due in two to three weeks, all of it inside the larger $10.00-$12.50 range. The honest conclusion is that I cannot call direction — the dojis and spinning tops say stalemate — so the right strategy is non-directional: bracket the triangle. Buy-stop at $11.90 on a close above $11.80, sell-stop at $10.10 on a close below $10.20, both requiring volume at least 1.75x the 20-day average to filter head fakes. The triangle's roughly $4.00 height projects to $15.80 on a bullish break, conveniently near the unfilled $15.50 earnings gap, while a breakdown targets the $7.50 all-time-low region. Stops reference the $10.90 point of control. I'd put 80% odds on a breakout within three to four weeks with direction a coin flip, and rate conviction for a large move very high, 9 of 10.

The prompt asks me to be critical of this ROKU divergence rather than just describe it, so I want to stress-test it. The raw signal is clean: price stepped from $105.20 to $108.50, a higher high, while RSI peaked at 74.1 on the first top but only 69.8 on the second (now 64.2), and the MACD line made +3.10 then just +2.60, with a bearish crossover two sessions back. Divergences fail constantly in strong uptrends, though, so what would make this one credible? Volume — and here it delivers: the new high came on lighter volume with OBV failing to confirm, which smells like distribution into strength. Add the rejection at the upper Bollinger Band near $109.10, a bearish candle at the peak, Stochastic crossing down from overbought at 75.8, and a potential double top with the trough at $98.00. The one genuine counterweight is ADX at 38.5 — still a strong trend, only just ticking down from 42, with +DI at 28.9 above -DI at 18.1. Shorting into that is how divergence trades die. The resolution is to demand price confirmation: no entry until a daily close below $100.00, which breaks both the psychological level and effectively the 20-day EMA at $99.80. Stop above $108.50, since a new high invalidates everything. Targets at $94.50, where the 50-day EMA meets the 61.8% Fibonacci, then $88.20 at the 200-day EMA — from a $99.90 entry that's 1.36:1 to the second target, acceptable rather than great. So: high-probability setup, yes, but only with confirmation. Conviction medium-high, 7 of 10 now, rising to 9 on a confirmed break of $100.

On XOM's weekly chart I'm being asked about a major reversal, so the bar is higher than for a daily-chart pullback call. The evidence starts with a long-cycle divergence: price made a new high at $123.75 four weeks ago, but the weekly MACD peaked at only +4.55 versus +6.20 at the prior high eight months back, and RSI printed 68.5 against 74.2 at the earlier $119.90 top — Class A bearish divergences on both. MACD has since crossed down (now +3.12 versus a +3.88 signal), the RSI broke its nine-month uptrend line, Parabolic SAR flipped to a sell at $123.90, and price just closed under the 20-week EMA at $115.50. What restrains me is the long-term structure: the 50-week SMA at $108.10 and 200-week at $85.40 are still rising, so this could just be a routine pause in a bull run. ADX at 23.1 flattening suggests the trend is losing definition rather than violently reversing, and the macro wildcard — crude reclaiming $85 WTI — would invalidate everything. The resolution is to stage the trade: initial short near $114.50 on the break of the 20-week EMA, add only on a decisive loss of $108.00, with targets at $109.80, $104.00, and the $95.80 double-top neckline, and a measured-move projection to $67.85 only if that neckline fails. Stop at $120.50, giving $6.00 of risk versus $18.70 to PT3, about 1:3.12. Using the 50-week MA as the confirmation gate resolves the trend conflict, and I'll set conviction for a three-to-six-month decline at 8 of 10.

ZS is an interesting case because the divergence the prompt asks about has already resolved — this is partly a post-mortem, partly a continuation trade. Over the past three months price topped near $255 in early February and made a lower high near $240 in late March, while MACD peaked at +8.5 then only +4.2, and RSI hit 75 then just 62. That divergence pair called the breakdown, and now the question is what to do at $193 with MACD deeply negative (-3.45 under a -2.81 signal) and price 10.2% below the 20-day EMA at $215.10, with a death cross imminent as the 50-day EMA ($228.40) bears down on the 200-day ($210.25). The tension is oversold risk: Stochastic at 18.5, CCI at -145.8, Williams %R at -88.2, and price hugging the lower Bollinger Band at $190.50. Normally those argue for a bounce, but ADX at 38.9 and rising with -DI at 35.1 dominating +DI at 12.4 says this is a walk down the band, and oversold can stay oversold in a trend this strong. So the primary trend outranks the oscillators. The plan: short into any bounce to the $200-$205 resistance zone (or aggressively near $193), targeting the $182.50 October low and then the $175.00 head-and-shoulders measured move, with the stop at $211.50 just above the 200-day EMA, since reclaiming that average is the one thing that breaks the thesis. From $200 that's risking $11.50 to make $17.50, about 1.52:1. I'd give continuation 70%, a bounce first 25%, and invalidation 5%, which lands conviction at high, 8 of 10.

SPOT's setup is defined by what's missing: volatility. Bollinger Band Width has collapsed to 0.04, a nine-month low, ATR is down to $7.15, its lowest in six months, and ADX at 14.8 confirms there is no trend to trade. MACD at +1.55 against a +1.48 signal with a +0.07 histogram, RSI pinned between 45 and 55 (now 51.2), Stochastic at 55.4, Williams %R at -48.2 — every momentum tool is shrugging. Price is coiled around the flat 20-day and 50-day EMAs at $312.50 and $309.80. When everything reads neutral like this, the neutrality itself is the signal: a squeeze this tight usually resolves violently, and the six-week symmetrical triangle (highs at $330 and $322 against lows at $295 and $304, apex in eight to ten sessions) gives me objective trigger lines. The judgment call is whether to lean directional. Price above the 200-day EMA at $255.10 and an intact uptrend line near $285 argue for a bullish tilt, but that's context, not a signal, so the honest answer is a dual-sided bracket. Long on a daily close above $321.00 with volume 1.5x average and ADX pushing through 20, stop $307.00, targets $331 then $346 on the measured move — risking $14 to make $25, about 1.79:1. Short on a close below $307.50, stop $321.50, targets $295 then $280. I'd handicap the upside break at 55% versus 45% down, a slight bullish edge from the long-term trend. Conviction that a big move is imminent: high, 8 of 10. Conviction on direction: genuinely neutral, 5 of 10.

PDD tagged $155.00 yesterday, a new high, and my job is to decide whether the momentum failure underneath it is tradable. The divergences check out on all three requested indicators: RSI printed 71.2 at $155 versus 78.9 at the $150 high eight days earlier, the MACD line peaked at +5.10 versus +6.25, and MFI diverged alongside OBV. The MACD histogram had already declined for five straight sessions before the peak, the bearish crossover fired one day ago (+4.52 under +4.88), and the candle at the high was a rejection off the upper Bollinger Band at $156.80 — a shooting star capping what looks like a rising wedge. The complication is that this is unambiguously a counter-trend short: every moving average slopes up, price sits 35.1% above the 200-day EMA at $114.72, and ADX at 48.5 marks a very strong trend, though it just ticked down for the first time in fifteen sessions and +DI has hooked lower. Counter-trend trades against an ADX near 50 demand a tight leash, so the stop goes just above the high at $156.00, roughly $8.00 of risk. Targets step down the structure: $144.15 at the 20-day SMA, $134.10 where the 50-day EMA meets the 38.2% Fibonacci, then $125.00 at the 61.8% retracement. Target 1 alone is a poor 0.5:1, so the trade only makes sense held to at least Target 2 at 1.75:1, ideally Target 3 at 2.88:1. With roughly 75% odds of reaching the 20-day SMA and 25% odds the divergence fails outright, I'll call this high conviction, 8 of 10, strictly as a tactical correction play.

Silver via SLV has spent six weeks going nowhere, and the compression statistics are extreme enough to build a trade around. Bollinger Band Width at 0.045 is in the 3rd percentile of the past year, ATR(14) at $0.35 is a 52-week low — just 1.5% of price — and ADX at 11.8 is about as trendless as markets get. The moving averages have converged into a 1.5% band (20-day EMA $22.85, 50-day $22.95, 200-day $22.70), MACD sits at +0.02 against a +0.01 signal, and RSI at 51.2 with Stochastic, CCI, and Williams %R all neutral means there is zero directional edge in the indicators. That's fine — for a squeeze play, balance is the setup. The six-week symmetrical triangle, descending from $24.10 and ascending from $22.05 with an apex due in seven to ten sessions, supplies the trigger lines. The only real decision is how to weight direction, and I'll give the bull side a modest edge, roughly 60/40, without pretending to certainty. Bullish plan: enter on a daily close above both the upper band and the triangle line near $23.45, volume at least 1.75x the 20-day average, stop $22.80 below the mid-band, targets $24.50 then $25.50 on the measured move — risking $0.65 to make $2.05, about 1:3.15. Bearish plan mirrors it: close below ~$22.30, stop $22.90 at the point of control, targets $21.50 then $20.75, roughly 1:2.58. The main hazard is a head fake through a band, which is exactly why both entries demand volume confirmation. Conviction a breakout comes within ten sessions: 9 of 10. Direction: 5 of 10 until price declares.

Boeing's daily chart is showing the skeleton of an inverse head and shoulders, and my task is to decide whether it's legitimate or wishful pattern-fitting. The structure maps cleanly: left shoulder near $175 in late April, head at $167.50 in mid-May, right shoulder building around $176, with a descending neckline near $182.50-$183.00. The validation the prompt demands comes from two places. First, oscillator divergence: at the head's lower low, RSI made a higher low (32.1 versus 28.5), a genuine bullish divergence, and RSI now sits at 54.2 above the midline. Second, momentum confirmation: MACD at -2.58 has crossed above its -3.15 signal with an expanding +0.57 histogram, the DI lines just flipped (+DI 26.8 over -DI 25.1) while ADX at 28.9 flattens, and OBV supports accumulation. The friction is overhead supply — price is testing the 50-day SMA at $180.50 and remains far below the 200-day at $205.10, so this is a bottoming attempt inside a larger downtrend. That means the pattern must prove itself; I won't front-run the neckline. Entry only on a daily close above $183.50, which filters intraday fakeouts. The pattern height of $15 ($182.50 minus $167.50) projects to $198.50, with $192.00 as an interim target at prior resistance. Stop below the right shoulder at $174.50, so I'm risking $9.00 to make $15.00, about 1:1.67. I'd put 65% odds on the neckline breaking within ten sessions and 70% on the measured move completing after that, which supports medium-high conviction, 7 of 10, entirely contingent on a volume-confirmed breakout.

Six months of AMD daily bars, and the dominant structure I keep coming back to is a head and shoulders top: left shoulder at $180.50 in early March, head at the $184.90 all-time high in mid-April, and a right shoulder that peaked around $178.20 last week. The detail that gives the pattern credibility is volume — the right shoulder formed on notably lighter volume than the head, exactly what distribution should look like. The indicator backdrop is consistent with topping rather than trending: MACD at +1.5 is still above its +0.8 signal but the histogram has fallen for five sessions with a bearish divergence against price, RSI at 58.2 couldn't reach 70 on the latest peak, ADX has slipped to 23.1 with +DI (25.5) and -DI (20.1) converging, and ATR at $5.80 has been declining for a month. The tension is that nothing has actually broken: price still holds above the 20-day EMA at $165.10 and 50-day at $160.30, and the 200-day SMA at $135.80 confirms the long-term uptrend. So the whole thesis is conditional on the neckline at $158.00-$160.00. If it breaks, the measured move is $184.90 minus $159.00, or $25.90 of height, projecting to $133.10 — which conveniently lands near the 200-day SMA, with $150.00 as an interim psychological stop. Invalidation is a close above the right shoulder at $178.50 (or $185.00 for aggressive entries). The conservative-entry math is mediocre, roughly 1:1.22, so sizing should be modest. I'd assign 65-70% odds of completion after a decisive break and call conviction moderate-high, 7 of 10, pending confirmation.

SPOT's bottoming structure is about as textbook as inverse head and shoulders patterns get, so my main job is stress-testing the confirmation evidence rather than the identification. The components: left shoulder at $152.00 in late August, capitulation head at $145.50 in mid-September, right shoulder low at $154.50 last week — a proper higher low — and a descending neckline in the $165.00-$166.00 zone. Volume behaves the way the pattern requires, contracting through the right shoulder with expansion on up-days. Momentum agrees: MACD crossed bullishly below zero (+1.25 over +0.98, histogram +0.27 and expanding), RSI has climbed from 34 at the head to 58.2, CCI has pushed through +100, and +DI (24.5) has crossed above -DI (19.8) with ADX at 18.9 just starting to lift. Price has reclaimed both the 20-day EMA at $155.10 and 50-day at $158.40. The complication is that the neckline sits almost exactly at the 200-day SMA ($165.50), stacking the pattern trigger on top of the single most-watched long-term resistance. Rather than treating that as a problem, I'll fold it into the trigger: entry requires a decisive close above both, which screens out weak pokes. The head-to-neckline height of $20 projects a target of $186.50 from a $166.50 breakout, with $188.00 (the prior swing high) as the stretch target, reachable in four to six weeks. Stop at $157.50 below the 50-day EMA and the right-shoulder swing, risking $9.00 against $20.00 — about 1:2.22. The bull-trap scenario, a low-volume pop over the neckline that fails, is the check on being wrong. Conviction: high, 8 of 10, contingent on the breakout actually printing.

PLTR has spent six weeks correcting, and the question is whether the oscillators are quietly signaling the turn before price does. The divergence evidence is real: price undercut to $20.25 last week versus $21.50 four weeks ago, yet RSI printed 29 at the new low against 25 at the old one — a Class A bullish divergence — and the MACD low of -1.50 was shallower than the prior -1.75. MACD has since crossed bullishly below zero (-0.85 over -1.15) with the histogram rising for seven straight days, Stochastic is at 65.2 climbing out of oversold, and CCI has cleared -100. RSI has also broken its own downtrend line, which usually leads price. The problem is the trend structure: price is only now testing the 20-day EMA at $22.10 from below, sits under the 50-day at $23.50, and the 20 is below the 50 — the lagging indicators still say downtrend, with only the 200-day EMA at $19.80 supporting from beneath. Divergences fail regularly when traders front-run them, so the answer is a scaled, confirmation-based entry: partial positions as price reclaims the EMAs, full size only on a break of the inverse head-and-shoulders neckline at $24.00. Targets ladder at $23.50 (50-day EMA), $26.00 (prior swing high), and $27.75 (the measured move, $24.00 plus the $3.75 pattern height). Stop at $19.95, below both the $20.25 head and the 200-day EMA. From a $21.80 entry that's $1.85 of risk against $4.20 to Target 2, about 2.27:1. I'd weight bullish reversal at 65%, range at 25%, breakdown at 10%, and set conviction moderate-high, 7 of 10.

DOCN has been bleeding, and I'm scanning specifically for divergence evidence that the decline is exhausting. It's there, and it's classic rather than hidden: the recent low at $32.10 undercut the $34.50 low from 18 days earlier, but RSI read 28.5 at the new low versus 24.0 at the old one, and the MACD histogram bottomed at -1.10 versus -2.45. Momentum made higher lows into lower prices on both indicators. Supporting details accumulate: a bullish MACD crossover four days ago below zero (-1.25 over -1.55), a capitulation poke below the lower Bollinger Band at the final low followed by a reversal back inside, a bullish engulfing candle, OBV divergence, and -DI (35.1) starting to converge toward +DI (15.2) as ADX at 38.5 flattens. The counterweight is severe: price trades below every moving average — 20-day EMA $35.80, 50-day $38.90, 200-day SMA $45.20 — and a death cross printed 45 days ago, so I'm calling a bottom inside a confirmed downtrend. Divergences in that context mark tradable lows, not necessarily new bull markets, so targets should respect overhead supply. The plan offers two entries: aggressive around $33.50 on the strength of the signals, conservative on a close above the 20-day EMA near $35.80. Targets at $37.70 (the double-bottom neckline), $41.50 (38.2% Fibonacci), and $45.20 (200-day SMA). Stop at $31.90 just under the low, so the aggressive entry risks $1.60 against $4.20 to the first target, a clean 2.6:1. Failure to reclaim the 20-day EMA on volume is the tell that I'm wrong. Conviction: high, 7.5 of 10.

For this AMD divergence scan I'm working across three oscillators the prompt names — RSI, MACD, MFI — and the story they tell is consistent. Price made a higher high at $184.92 last week, but the MACD line peaked at +5.20 versus +6.80 back when the stock was at $178, and RSI printed 68.5 at the new high against 75.3 at the prior one. MFI failed to confirm as well, and OBV backs the divergence set. The bearish crossover four sessions ago (MACD +3.52 under a +4.11 signal, histogram negative and growing) plus a slip below the middle Bollinger Band at $176.50 says the correction may already be underway. What forces care here is the trend context: the 50-day EMA at $164.30 and 200-day at $135.80 both slope up, and ADX at 38.9 marks a still-strong trend, though it just curled down from 42.5 while -DI (22.1) rises against +DI (28.5). Oscillator sell signals in trending markets are notorious for producing false exits, so the trade needs a structural trigger, not just indicator pessimism. The plan: short only on a daily close below the 23.6% Fibonacci level at $172.50, stop at $181.50 above the psychological $180 area, targets at $164.80 where the 38.2% retracement meets the 50-day EMA, then $158.50 at the 50% level. The ratios are modest — roughly 1.1:1 to the first target, 1.5:1 to the second — so this is a probability trade, and I'd put 70% odds on reaching Target 1 within one to two months. Medium-term correction, not trend reversal, is the framing, and conviction lands at 7.5 of 10.

MU just surged, and the prompt wants me to interrogate the volume rather than the price. The volume evidence is the strongest part of the picture: the breakout from the six-month cup and handle (cup between $68 and $90, handle $84-$89, breakout at $90) came with a genuine volume spike, and — more importantly — OBV is making new highs ahead of price, which is what institutional accumulation looks like. CMF confirms positive money flow. The indicator suite is uniformly strong: MACD +2.15 over a +1.88 signal with a widening histogram, ADX at 41.5 with +DI (38.9) dwarfing -DI (13.2), price walking the upper Bollinger Band at $95.80 with bandwidth in the 85th percentile, and ATR expanding from $1.90 to $2.85. The honest tension is the overbought stack: RSI 74.2, Stochastic 91.5, Williams %R at -7.8. In a weaker tape those would be sell signals, but there's no bearish divergence — price and RSI are making highs together — and in a volume-confirmed breakout, overbought readings are a feature of momentum, not a top. So I resolve the conflict in favor of the volume evidence and treat pullbacks as entries rather than exits. Strategy: buy dips toward the low-$90s, ideally near $93, with the volume-profile gap suggesting little resistance until $100. Targets at $100 (psychological) and $112 (cup depth of $22 added to $90). Stop at $88.90, below the breakout and the gap. From $93 that's $4.10 of risk against 1.71:1 to the first target and 4.63:1 to the second. Roughly 75% odds of $100 within one to three months. Conviction: very high, 9 of 10.

Block's rally to $82.50 is the thing under examination, and the exhaustion evidence the prompt asks about is present on all three requested oscillators. RSI peaked at 74.1 at the $82.50 high, below its 78.5 peak from early March when price was only $79.00; the MACD topped at +2.80 versus +4.10 at that earlier, lower price high; MFI diverged too, and volume failed to expand into the latest high. MACD has now crossed bearishly (+2.15 under +2.50), Stochastic is rolling down from overbought at 65.4, CCI has fallen from +180 to +95.2, and the last three sessions look like the start of three black crows. Price action adds a rising wedge over six weeks with the lower trendline near $76.00. The genuine complication is the recent Golden Cross — the 50-day EMA ($71.20) crossing above the 200-day ($65.40) — a long-term bullish signal sitting directly against these medium-term bearish reads. I resolve that by time horizon: the divergences and wedge are immediate and actionable, while the Golden Cross mostly tells me where deeper support lives. So: short on a daily close below $76.00, stop above the high at $83.50, targets at $71.20 (50-day EMA), $68.00 (prior resistance), and $65.40 (200-day EMA). The math to Target 1 is admittedly poor — $7.50 risk against $4.80, about 0.64:1 — so the trade only earns its keep aiming at Target 2 or beyond. With roughly 70% odds of reaching the 50-day EMA within one to two months after confirmation, conviction sits at 7.5 of 10, strictly contingent on the $76.00 break.

CAT's uptrend has been powerful, but the prompt flags momentum loss, and the divergence work bears that out. Price stepped up to $365.20 last week, yet the MACD line peaked at only +4.80 versus a prior +6.20, and RSI printed 68 at the new high versus 79 a month ago — a multi-week Class A bearish divergence on both, with the Stochastic trending down from overbought at 45.2 without having confirmed the high either. The bearish MACD crossover three sessions back (+4.52 under +5.11, histogram -0.59) adds a timing element. My hesitation mirrors every counter-trend setup: ADX at 38.5 still reads strong-trend, price holds above the 20-day EMA at $354.10 and 50-day at $342.50, and the 200-day at $305.80 confirms a healthy long-term uptrend. Divergences alone don't justify shorting a name like this — an infrastructure headline could erase the signal in a session, which is exactly the failure mode I noted. What makes it tradable is structure: a double top at $360 and $365.20 with the neckline at the $348.00 intervening low. That gives a price-based confirmation gate. Short only on a daily close below $348.00, stop at $358.50 above the midpoint of the decline, targets at $342.50 (50-day EMA) then $330.00 (measured move and major support). From a $347.90 fill that's $10.60 of risk against $17.90 to Target 2, about 1.69:1.
